name: Multiple sclerosis
description: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating disease of the central nervous system, in which peripheral autoimmunity gives way over time to compartmentalised CNS inflammation, failed remyelination, and progressive axonal loss.

vocabulary.risk_weights_rationale: How strongly each domain constrains combination use in this population. Infection and autoimmunity dominate because the therapies are chronic immunosuppressants given to young adults over decades; teratogenicity is weighted lower than its clinical seriousness because it is manageable by prescribing policy rather than by drug choice.

delivery.sanctuary_rationale: Every approved disease-modifying therapy acts largely in the periphery, and every one of them plateaus in progressive disease. The leading explanation is that inflammation behind a re-closed blood-brain barrier becomes self-sustaining and inaccessible to peripheral immunosuppression. A molecule designed for progressive MS therefore has to reach CNS parenchyma at therapeutic exposure, which makes the CNS multi-parameter score a gate rather than a preference.

provenance.note: Discovery-stage research context. Nothing derived from it is a clinical recommendation.
